metric.name: frame_p95_ms
metric.sql_used:
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.frames.timeline;
WITH
  window_frames AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT f.upid, f.ui_thread_utid, a.id, a.dur, a.jank_type
    FROM android_frames_layers AS f
    JOIN actual_frame_timeline_slice AS a ON a.id = f.actual_frame_timeline_id
    WHERE f.layer_name NOT GLOB '*SurfaceView*' AND a.dur > 0
  ),
  app AS (
    SELECT upid FROM window_frames GROUP BY upid ORDER BY count(*) DESC, upid LIMIT 1
  ),
  frames AS (
    SELECT * FROM window_frames WHERE upid = (SELECT upid FROM app)
  ),
  ranked AS (
    SELECT dur AS ns, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY dur) AS rank, count(*) OVER () AS n
    FROM frames
  )
SELECT (SELECT ns / 1e6 FROM ranked WHERE rank = (n * 95 + 99) / 100) AS value

claims.text: The selected frame-duration metric improved: p95 frame time decreased from 76.544292 ms in the baseline to 73.255125 ms in the current trace.

claims.text: The range contains the feed collector comment change, a state-variable rename, a handler rename, and the TV-controls timeout change; none provides trace evidence of a frame-time regression, so no culprit is attributed.

caveats: This conclusion is based on one capture per side, so small changes can be run-to-run noise.
The current trace metadata identifies an emulator (sdk_gphone64_arm64, SDK 36) and a non-debuggable benchmark build.
Some whole-trace wait metrics increased, but they are exposure-sensitive and do not outweigh the improved frame-duration metrics for this diagnosis.
